question: Should Crabbox sponsor a customer-hosted Cloud Run sandbox bridge as a separately named built-in delegated provider?
rationale: Cloud Run supplies an in-service execution primitive rather than a standalone lease, so support commits the project to a deployment, IAM, authentication, transport, and lifecycle contract that current policy does not choose automatically.

options.title: Sponsor bounded external prototype
options.body: Validate deployment, authenticated invocation, file transfer, status, stop, and cleanup through the external-provider contract before considering built-in registration.

options.title: Sponsor built-in provider spike
options.body: Design and prove a first-class delegated provider immediately under a distinct provider name.

options.title: Defer preview support
options.body: Wait for Google to expose a stable standalone remote sandbox lifecycle that maps more directly to Crabbox.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bounded external prototype
recommendation.body: Validate deployment, authenticated invocation, file transfer, status, stop, and cleanup through the external-provider contract before considering built-in registration.

likelyOwner.reason: Current provider-framework, lifecycle-policy, and release history makes him the strongest available owner for the product-sponsorship decision.
